text:
maya: Pushed cryptography 3.4.8 across API + worker canaries in us-west-2. Starting validation checklist — smoke, perf, KMS access, RBAC/audit log sanity. @nathan @samir please run smoke+perf and watch key access logs.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary-redwood-api v2026.03.20-cryptopatch (canary=us-west-2)

maya: Smoke script I usually run: `./scripts/smoke.sh --target canary --count 200 --parallel 4` (hits /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings).

nathan: Running smoke now. Will also tail audit logs to confirm KMS key usage entries.

nathan: Quick check — k8s secret mount ok, key client initialized. Starting traffic.

samir: Smoke results after first 200 req: 2xx=198, 5xx=2 (~1% error). Errors are 500s from key client layer.

tara: Can you paste the error lines?

samir: Log snippet:```
ERROR keyclient: failed GetKey version=2026-01-15 err="rpc: deadline exceeded"
stack: keyclient/request.go:42
```
Also seeing p50 +10ms, p95 +120ms vs baseline for API.

nathan: Audit logs show repeated GetKey calls for the same key with many short-lived connections — entries exist, RBAC looks fine. So not permission denied, looks like timeouts/retries to KMS.

maya: Ok — hypothesis: new lib changed TLS handshake/conn reuse behaviour causing KMS latency spikes. Ops decision: keep canary but shift traffic: route 80% canary, 20% baseline for 30m. If errors >0.5% or p95 regresses >50ms -> rollback.

deploy-bot: traffic-split applied: canary=80%, baseline=20% (route policy: canary-cryptopatch)

samir: Kicking off perf harness: `./bench/perf_compare.sh --baseline=stable --candidate=canary --rps=200 --duration=10m`

yara: Monitoring panels to watch: `api.latency.p95`, `keyclient.calls_failed`, `k8s.container_cpu`; setting alert: `keyclient_err_rate > 0.5% for 5m` -> pager.

tara: Perf summary (initial): p50 baseline 38ms -> canary 50ms; p95 baseline 230ms -> canary 305ms; 99th baseline 520ms -> canary 560ms. No CPU diff; keyclient retries higher.

nathan: Repro curl to exercise KMS call:```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://kms.internal/key/foo?version=latest
```
I can see occasional TLS renegotiation logs on the keyserver side.

maya: Mitigations to consider: 1) bump keyclient timeout + enable keepalive, 2) add local short-lived cache for key metadata, 3) revert cryptography bump and re-evaluate. Which is lowest customer-risk?

samir: Lowest-risk immediate fix: increase client timeout 500ms -> 1200ms and enable conn reuse/keepalive. Deploy that to canary, re-run smoke/perf. If fixes, escalate with KMS team for handshake tuning.

nathan: Pushing small canary patch with timeout bump + keepalive flag now.

ops-ci: CI job: canary-patch-timeout applied to deployment redwood-api-canary (image: v2026.03.20-cryptopatch-timeout).

nathan: Running smoke again. `./scripts/smoke.sh --target canary --count 200`

nathan: Smoke results: 200/200 2xx, 0 errors. p95 now ~+20ms over baseline. No 5xx.

yara: Alerts: nothing fired. Dashboard panels normalized. Keeping traffic split for another 15m for observation.

maya: Good. If next 45m stable we plan staged rollout to eu-west-1 then ap-southeast-1. Also open PR to update dependency notes and add a short post-patch validation checklist in the repo (smoke commands, perf scripts, grafana queries, alert knobs).

tara: I'll draft a short incident note capturing hypothesis (TLS handshake/conn reuse), mitigation (timeout bump + keepalive), tests run, and followups (KMS ticket to investigate handshake frequency + caching options).

maya: Thanks all — leave on-watch. If anything regresses we roll back per the earlier threshold. Closing thread in 1h if everything stays green. :white_check_mark:
